fact: Complement is a major effector mechanism of humoral immunity and also an important effector mechanism of innate immunity.
quote: one of the major effector mechanisms of humoral immunity and is also an important effector mechanism of innate immunity

fact: Complement proteases circulate as inactive zymogens and become active only after proteolytic cleavage.
quote: synthesized as inactive pro-enzymes, or zymogens, which only become enzymatically active after proteolytic cleavage

fact: Each activated complement protease cleaves many molecules of the next zymogen, so the signal amplifies at each step.
quote: each becoming an active protease that cleaves and activates many molecules of the next zymogen in the pathway

fact: The larger cleavage fragment gets the suffix b and the smaller fragment gets the suffix a; C2 is the one exception.
quote: The larger fragment is always designated by the suffix b, with one exception.

fact: For C2, the larger fragment that stays attached is called C2a and the released smaller fragment is called C2b.
quote: because the attached, larger fragment is called the a piece and the released part is the b fragment

fact: The reaction sequence of the classical pathway is C1, C4, C2, C3, C5, C6, C7, C8 and C9.
quote: example, is Cl, C4, C2, C3, C5, C6, C7, C8, and C9

fact: Three pathways activate complement: the classical pathway (antibody bound to antigen), the alternative pathway (microbial surfaces without antibody) and the lectin pathway (lectins that bind microbial carbohydrates).
quote: the classical pathway, which is activated by certain classes of antibodies bound to antigens; the alternative pathway

fact: The alternative and lectin pathways are innate effector mechanisms; the classical pathway is a major mechanism of adaptive humoral immunity.
quote: The alternative and lectin pathways are effector mechanisms of innate immunity, whereas the classical pathway is a major mechanism of adaptive humoral immunity.

fact: All three pathways can start without antibody, as part of innate immunity.
quote: All three pathways can be initiated independently of antibody as part of innate immunity.

fact: The central event of complement activation is cleavage of C3 by a C3 convertase into C3a and C3b, with covalent attachment of C3b to the target surface.
quote: The central event in complement activation is proteolysis of the complement protein C3

fact: Cleavage of C3 exposes a reactive thioester bond in C3b; if C3b does not bond to a nearby surface, the thioester is hydrolyzed and C3b becomes inactive.
quote: If no bond is made, the thioester is rapidly hydrolyzed, inactivating C3b.

fact: Regulatory proteins on normal host cells inhibit complement activation; microbes lack these proteins, so activation proceeds on microbial surfaces.
quote: Complement activation is inhibited by regulatory proteins that are present on normal host cells and absent from microbes.

fact: The classical pathway starts when C1 binds the CH2 domain of IgG or the CH3 domain of IgM that has bound antigen.
quote: binding of the complement protein C1 to the CH2 domains of IgG or the CH3 domains of IgM

fact: Among human IgG subclasses, IgG1 and IgG3 are the most efficient complement activators.
quote: Among IgG antibodies, IgG1 and IgG3 (in humans) are more efficient activators of complement than are other subclasses.

fact: IgG2 activates complement weakly and IgG4 does not activate complement.
quote: IgG2 has some ability to activate complement, but IgG4 does not.

fact: C1 consists of C1q, which binds antibody, and C1r and C1s, which are serine proteases.
quote: C1q binds to the antibody, and C1r and C1s are proteases

fact: Each C1q must bind at least two Ig heavy chains to be activated, so only antigen-bound antibody, not free antibody, activates the classical pathway.
quote: each C1q molecule must bind to at least two Ig heavy chains to be activated

fact: One antigen-bound IgM molecule can bind two or more C1q molecules, so IgM fixes complement more efficiently than IgG.
quote: a single molecule of IgM can bind two or more C1q molecules

fact: C1q also binds pentraxins such as C-reactive protein (CRP) and serum amyloid P, and it binds apoptotic bodies.
quote: C1q also binds to pentraxins like C-reactive protein and serum amyloid protein, and can also bind to apoptotic bodies

fact: Binding of C1q activates C1r; C1r cleaves and activates C1s; C1s cleaves C4 to C4b.
quote: enzymatic activation of the associated C1r, which cleaves and activates C1s

fact: C2 binds surface C4b and is cleaved by C1s; the larger C2a fragment stays bound to C4b.
quote: a larger C2a fragment that remains physically associated with C4b on the cell surface

fact: C4b2a is the classical pathway C3 convertase.
quote: The resulting C4b2a complex is the classical pathway C3 convertase

fact: C3b binds to C4b2a to form C4b2a3b, the classical pathway C5 convertase.
quote: form a C4b2a3b complex. This complex functions as the classical pathway C5 convertase

fact: C3 is homologous to C4, and factor B is homologous to C2.
quote: C3 in the alternative pathway is homologous to C4 in the classical pathway, and Factor B is homologous to C2.

fact: The lectin pathway starts when plasma mannose-binding lectin (MBL) or ficolins bind microbial polysaccharides.
quote: triggered by the binding of microbial polysaccharides to circulating lectins, such as plasma mannose-binding lectin (MBL), or to ficolins

fact: MBL binds mannose residues on microbial polysaccharides.
quote: MBL binds to mannose residues on polysaccharides

fact: Ficolins (L-, H- and M-ficolin) bind N-acetylglucosamine-containing glycans through a fibrinogen-like domain.
quote: the fibrinogen-like domain of ficolin binds N-acetylglucosamine–containing glycans

fact: MASP1 may activate MASP2, and MASP2 cleaves C4 and C2.
quote: MASP1 may activate MASP2 and MASP2 is the protease that cleaves C4 and C2

fact: The lectin pathway forms the same C3 convertase as the classical pathway, C4b2a.
quote: forming C4b2a, which is the C3 convertase of the lectin pathway

fact: Plasma C3 is cleaved spontaneously at a low rate of 1-2% of total C3 per hour (C3 tick-over).
quote: continuously cleaved at a low rate (1%–2% of the total plasma C3 per hour)

fact: Tick-over gives C3(H2O), which binds factor B; factor D then cleaves factor B and a short-lived fluid-phase C3 convertase, C3(H2O)Bb, forms.
quote: producing a short-lived fluid-phase C3 convertase, C3(H,O)Bb

fact: Surface C3b binds factor B, factor D cleaves factor B (Ba is released, Bb stays), and C3bBb forms the alternative pathway C3 convertase.
quote: The C3bBb complex is the alternative pathway C3 convertase

fact: The alternative pathway C3 convertase amplifies complement activation that starts by the alternative, classical or lectin pathway.
quote: the alternative pathway C3 convertase functions to amplify complement activation when it is initiated by the alternative, classical, or lectin pathway

fact: Factor D is the only activating protease of complement that circulates as an active enzyme, not as a zymogen.
quote: the only activating protease of the complement system to circulate as an active enzyme rather than a zymogen

fact: Properdin binds and stabilizes C3bBb, and it attaches preferentially to microbial surfaces.
quote: properdin, can bind to and stabilize the C3bBb complex, and the attachment of properdin is favored on microbial as opposed to normal host cells

fact: The alternative pathway C5 convertase contains one Bb and two C3b molecules (C3bBb3b).
quote: a complex containing one Bb moiety and two molecules of C3b, which functions as the alternative pathway C5 convertase

fact: Janeway writes the C5 convertases as C4b2a3b (classical and lectin) and C3b2Bb (alternative).
quote: C3b binds both to C4b2a and C3bBb, forming the active C5 convertases C4b2a3b and C3b,Bb

fact: C5 binds to the C3b part of a C5 convertase and is cleaved by C2a or Bb.
quote: rendered susceptible to cleavage by the serine protease activity of C2a or Bb

fact: Unlike C3b and C4b, C5b does not bind covalently to the cell surface.
quote: Unlike C3b and C4b, C5b is not covalently bound to the cell surface.

fact: C5b binds C6 and then C7; the C5b-7 complex inserts into the lipid bilayer.
quote: C7 from the plasma then binds to the α chain of C5b and forms the C5b-C6-C7 (C5b-7) complex

fact: C8 binds to form C5b-8, which makes small, unstable pores of 0.4-3 nm.
quote: forms unstable pores that range from 0.4 to 3 nm in diameter

fact: Recruitment of the first C9 molecule is the rate-limiting step of MAC formation.
quote: The rate-limiting step in MAC formation is the recruitment of the first C9 molecule

fact: Abbas states that the MAC pore contains C5b, C6, C7, C8 and up to 18 C9 molecules.
quote: C5b-9 complexes containing C5b, C6, C7, C8, and up to 18 molecules of C9

fact: Janeway states that 10-16 C9 molecules polymerize to form the MAC.
quote: the polymerization of 10-16 molecules of C9

fact: Water enters through the MAC pore, and the cell swells and ruptures (osmotic lysis).
quote: The entry of water results in osmotic swelling and rupture of the cells

fact: MAC-mediated lysis is critical for defense against only a few pathogens, such as thin-walled Neisseria.
quote: such as bacteria of the genus Neisseria, which have thin cell walls

fact: Deficiency of C5-C9 is associated with susceptibility only to Neisseria species.
quote: deficiencies in complement components C5-C9 have been associated with susceptibility only to Neisseria species

fact: C3b and C4b bind CR1; iC3b binds CR3 (MAC-1) and CR4.
quote: C3b and C4b (the latter generated by the classical pathway only) bind to CR1, and iC3b binds to CR3 (MAC-1) and CR4

fact: CR1 alone triggers phagocytosis of C3b-coated microbes inefficiently; simultaneous IgG binding to Fc gamma receptors enhances it.
quote: By itself, CR1 is inefficient at inducing the phagocytosis of C3b-coated microbes

fact: Binding of iC3b to CR3 is sufficient on its own to stimulate phagocytosis.
quote: the binding of iC3b to the receptor CR3 is sufficient on its own to stimulate phagocytosis

fact: People without a spleen are susceptible to disseminated pneumococcal and meningococcal septicemia.
quote: are susceptible to disseminated pneumococcal and meningococcal septicemia

fact: C5a, C4a and C3a bind to mast cells and cause degranulation with release of vasoactive mediators such as histamine.
quote: All three peptides bind to mast cells and induce degranulation, with the release of vasoactive mediators, such as histamine.

fact: C3a, C4a and C5a are called anaphylatoxins because the mast cell reactions they trigger are characteristic of anaphylaxis.
quote: These peptides are also called anaphylatoxins because the mast cell reactions they trigger are characteristic of anaphylaxis

fact: C5a is the most potent mediator of mast cell degranulation; C3a is about 20-fold and C4a about 2500-fold less potent.
quote: C5a is the most potent mediator of mast cell degranulation, C3a is approximately 20-fold less potent, and C4a is approximately 2500-fold less

fact: In neutrophils, C5a stimulates motility, firm adhesion to endothelium and, at high doses, the respiratory burst.
quote: C5a stimulates motility, firm adhesion to endothelial cells, and, at high doses, stimulation of the respiratory burst

fact: Large systemic amounts of anaphylatoxins cause circulatory collapse, a shock-like syndrome similar to a systemic IgE-mediated allergic reaction.
quote: they induce a generalized circulatory collapse, producing a shock-like syndrome similar to that seen in a systemic allergic reaction

fact: C3a and C5a can degranulate mast cells without allergen cross-linking of the high-affinity IgE receptor.
quote: The complement fragments C3a and C5a can cause mast cell degranulation, and this is why they were named anaphylatoxins.

fact: C5a is a chemoattractant for eosinophils.
quote: the complement product C5a and the lipid mediators PAF and LTB4 produced by mast cells also function as chemoattractants for eosinophils

fact: The C5a receptor C5aR1 is a G protein-coupled receptor on neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils, monocytes, macrophages, mast cells and other cells.
quote: C5aR1, is the most thoroughly characterized. It is a member of the G protein–coupled receptor family

fact: Plasma carboxypeptidases remove the C-terminal arginine of C3a and C5a; the des-Arg forms keep only about 10% of the activity.
quote: C3a des-Arg and C5a des-Arg, which each have only approximately 10% of the activity of the native forms

fact: CR1 on erythrocytes binds circulating immune complexes that carry C3b and C4b and carries them to the liver and spleen for removal by phagocytes.
quote: CR1 on erythrocytes binds circulating immune complexes with attached C3b and C4b

fact: CR2 (CD21) binds C3d, C3dg and iC3b; on B cells it forms a complex with CD19 and CD81.
quote: a trimolecular complex that includes two other noncovalently attached proteins called CD19 and CD81

fact: CR2 is the receptor for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV).
quote: Receptor for EBV

fact: C3d on an antigen binds CR2 on B cells and facilitates B-cell activation.
quote: The C3d protein generated from C3 binds to CR2 on B cells and facilitates B-cell activation

fact: CR3 (MAC-1, CD11b/CD18) is an integrin that binds iC3b and also ICAM-1 on endothelium.
quote: The type 3 complement receptor, also called MAC-1 (CR3, CD11bCD18), is an integrin

fact: CR4 (CD11c/CD18) also binds iC3b; CD11c is a marker of dendritic cells.
quote: CD11c is abundantly expressed on dendritic cells and is used as a marker for this cell type.

fact: Mutations in the shared CD18 chain remove CR3 and CR4 and cause leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD).
quote: The disease caused by this gene defect is called leukocyte adhesion deficiency

fact: C1 inhibitor (C1-INH) is a serpin; active C1r2s2 cleaves it, it binds covalently, and C1r2s2 dissociates from C1q.
quote: C1 INH is a serine protease inhibitor (serpin) that mimics the normal substrates of C1r and C1s

fact: C1-INH also inactivates MASP2 and so dampens the lectin pathway.
quote: by inactivating MASP2, C1-INH also dampens the lectin pathway

fact: C1-INH also inhibits kallikrein and coagulation factor XII, which promote bradykinin formation.
quote: C1-INH is an inhibitor of other plasma serine proteases besides C1, including kallikrein and coagulation factor XII

fact: Hereditary angioedema (HAE) is an autosomal dominant disease caused by deficiency of C1-INH.
quote: An autosomal dominant inherited disease called hereditary angioedema is due to a deficiency of C1-INH.

fact: The edema mediators in HAE include C2 kinin (a C2 fragment) and bradykinin.
quote: The mediators of edema formation in patients with hereditary angioedema include a proteolytic fragment of C2, called C2 kinin, and bradykinin.

fact: Factor H binds C3b, displaces Bb and is a cofactor for factor I-mediated cleavage of C3b.
quote: Binds C3b and displaces Bb

fact: Factor H blocks only Bb binding to C3b, so it regulates the alternative pathway but not the classical pathway.
quote: Factor H inhibits binding of only Bb to C3b and is thus a regulator of the alternative but not the classical pathway.

fact: Sialic acid-rich host cell surfaces favor binding of factor H over factor B.
quote: cell surfaces rich in sialic acid favor binding of the regulatory protein Factor H over the alternative pathway protein Factor B

fact: C4-binding protein (C4BP) is a plasma protein that binds C4b, displaces C2 and is a cofactor for factor I-mediated cleavage of C4b.
quote: Binds C4b and displaces C2

fact: Factor I is a plasma serine protease that cleaves C3b and C4b, with factor H, MCP, C4BP or CR1 as cofactor.
quote: cleaves C3b and C4b by using factor H, MCP, C4BP, or CR1 as cofactors

fact: Factor I circulates in active form but cleaves C3b and C4b only when they are bound to a cofactor protein.
quote: it circulates in active form but can cleave C3b and C4b only when they are bound to a membrane cofactor protein

fact: Factor I cleavage of C3b generates iC3b, C3d and C3dg; these do not take part in activation but bind receptors on phagocytes and B cells.
quote: Factor I–mediated cleavage of C3b generates the fragments called iC3b, C3d, and C3dg

fact: Membrane cofactor protein (MCP, CD46) is on leukocytes, epithelial cells and endothelial cells and is a cofactor for factor I cleavage of C3b and C4b.
quote: Cofactor for factor I–mediated cleavage of C3b and C4b

fact: Decay-accelerating factor (DAF, CD55) displaces C2a from C4b and Bb from C3b, so it dissociates both C3 convertases.
quote: Displaces C2a from C4b and Bb from C3b (dissociation of C3 convertases)

fact: CR1, DAF and factor H displace Bb from C3b; CR1, MCP and factor H are cofactors for factor I cleavage of C3b.
quote: CR1, DAF, and factor H displace Bb from C3b, and CR1, MCP, and factor H catalyze the cleavage of bound C3b

fact: CD59 is a GPI-linked membrane protein that incorporates into the assembling MAC after C5b-8 insertion and blocks addition of C9.
quote: It works by incorporating itself into assembling MACs after the membrane insertion of C5b-8, thereby inhibiting the subsequent addition of C9 molecules

fact: CD59 is also called protectin.
quote: CD59 or protectin, which inhibits the binding of C9 to the C5b678 complex

fact: Plasma S protein binds soluble C5b-7 complexes and prevents their insertion into bystander cell membranes.
quote: plasma proteins such as S protein, which functions by binding to soluble C5b,6,7 complexes

fact: S protein is also called vitronectin.
quote: vitronectin, also known as S-protein, bind to the C5b67 complex

fact: Failure to make GPI anchors removes DAF and CD59 from blood cells and causes paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH).
quote: results in the failure to express many GPI-linked membrane proteins, including DAF and CD59

fact: Factor I deficiency depletes plasma C3 through unregulated fluid-phase C3 convertase formation and causes pyogenic infections.
quote: In patients with Factor I deficiency, plasma C3 is depleted

fact: In complement-mediated hemolytic-uremic syndrome, the most common mutations are in the factor H gene; MCP mutations also occur.
quote: the most common mutations in this condition are in the Factor H gene

fact: Some microbes, such as Gram-positive bacteria and some fungi, have thick cell walls that prevent binding of complement proteins such as the MAC.
quote: Some microbes express thick cell walls that prevent the binding of complement proteins, such as the MAC.

fact: Many pathogens evade complement by recruiting host regulators, for example factor H through surface sialic acid.
quote: Microbes can evade the complement system by recruiting host complement regulatory proteins.

fact: Janeway states that iC3b is a ligand for CR2, CR3 and CR4, but not for CR1.
quote: producing iC3b, which is a ligand for the complement receptors CR2, CR3 and CR4, but not CR1

fact: Abbas lists the CR1 ligands as C3b > C4b > iC3b.
quote: C3b > C4b > iC3b

fact: In bacterial infection, alternative pathway activation releases C5a, which directly triggers mast cell degranulation.
quote: complement activation by the alternative pathway, leading to the release of C5a, which directly triggers mast cell degranulation

fact: IgM against capsular polysaccharides activates the classical pathway and causes phagocytic clearance of pneumococci and meningococci in the spleen.
quote: activate the classical pathway of complement, and cause phagocytic clearance of the bacteria in the spleen

fact: The most important action of complement is to help phagocytes take up and destroy pathogens.
quote: The most important action of complement is to facilitate the uptake and destruction of pathogens by phagocytic cells.

fact: Regulators act at three levels: they inhibit C3 convertase formation, break down C3 and C5 convertases, and inhibit MAC formation.
quote: Different regulatory mechanisms inhibit the formation of C3 convertases in the early steps of complement activation, break down and inactivate C3 and C5 convertases

fact: The reactive thioester of C3b and C4b cannot distinguish a host cell surface from a pathogen surface.
quote: has no mechanism for distinguishing an acceptor hydroxyl or amine group on a host cell from a similar group on the surface of a pathogen
